title: How to Choose Effective, Science-based Mental Health Apps, with Stephen Schueller, PhD

sentences.en: 2020 has been a watershed year in digital mental health care.
sentences.zh: 2020年是数字心理健康护理的分水岭之年。

sentences.en: The coronavirus pandemic and a summer of racial reckoning have left many Americans stressed, anxious, and depressed,
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情和夏季的种族清算运动让许多美国人感到压力、焦虑和抑郁，

sentences.en: while at the same time the pandemic has made it more difficult to obtain in-person mental health care.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，疫情也使得获取面对面的心理健康护理变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Can technology help to bridge that gap?
sentences.zh: 科技能帮助弥合这一差距吗？

sentences.en: Many consumers seem to think so.
sentences.zh: 许多消费者似乎认为可以。

sentences.en: One market research firm found that downloads of the top 20 mental wellness apps rose almost 30% from January to April this year.
sentences.zh: 一家市场研究公司发现，今年1月至4月，排名前20的心理健康应用程序的下载量增长了近30%。

sentences.en: But among the thousands of apps that aim to help people with everything from stress to anxiety to PTSD to sleep problems, how many are based on solid scientific research?
sentences.zh: 但在成千上万旨在帮助人们解决从压力、焦虑到创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）以及睡眠问题等各种困扰的应用程序中，有多少是基于扎实的科学研究的呢？

sentences.en: How many live up to what they promise?
sentences.zh: 又有多少能兑现它们的承诺？

sentences.en: And how can you as a consumer make informed choices based on your mental health needs?
sentences.zh: 作为消费者，你又该如何根据自己的心理健康需求做出明智的选择呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Stephen Shuler, executive director of One Mind Cyberguide,
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是One Mind Cyberguide的执行董事斯蒂芬·舒勒（Stephen Shuler）博士，

sentences.en: a nonprofit mental health app reviewing website that's been called the Consumer Reports of Digital Mental Health.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非营利性的心理健康应用程序评估网站，被称为“数字心理健康的《消费者报告》”。

sentences.en: He is also a professor in the Department of Social Ecology at the University of California, Irvine, where he works on developing and evaluating digital mental health technologies
sentences.zh: 他同时也是加州大学欧文分校社会生态学系的教授，致力于开发和评估数字心理健康技术，

sentences.en: with the goal of expanding access to mental health care.
sentences.zh: 目标是扩大心理健康护理的覆盖范围。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Shuler.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》，舒勒博士。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'm really excited to be on here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: As I just mentioned in the intro, One Mind Cyberguide has been called the Consumer Reports of Digital Mental Health.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才在介绍中提到的，One Mind Cyberguide被称为数字心理健康的《消费者报告》。

sentences.en: Why did it get that moniker?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有这个称号？

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: And is this something that we need out there in the marketplace?
sentences.zh: 这是否是我们市场上所需要的东西？

sentences.en: Well, so I definitely think it's something we need out there in the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我绝对认为这是我们市场上所需要的东西。

sentences.en: There are a host of different digital mental health products, most of these being apps.
sentences.zh: 市面上有大量不同的数字心理健康产品，其中大多数是应用程序。

sentences.en: So if you were to go to the app store and to put in the search box depression, anxiety, stress, PTSD, you would get tens of thousands of responses across those different terMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你去应用商店，在搜索框中输入“抑郁”、“焦虑”、“压力”、“PTSD”，你会得到成千上万条针对这些不同术语的搜索结果。

sentences.en: In fact, some estimates suggest that there's about 20 to 25,000 mental health apps that are out there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些估计显示，目前市面上大约有2万到2.5万个心理健康应用程序。

sentences.en: And trying to find a good one is like finding a needle in a haystack.
sentences.zh: 想要找到一个好的应用就像大海捞针一样。

sentences.en: And so definitely we find that a lot of consumers do need some help in terms of separating the good from the bad,
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实发现，许多消费者在区分好坏方面确实需要一些帮助，

sentences.en: the effective from the not effective, the science-backed from the ones that aren't science-backed.
sentences.zh: 区分有效的和无效的，有科学依据的和没有科学依据的。

sentences.en: And what we do at One Mind Cyberguide is we identify and we review products on multiple dimensions.
sentences.zh: 我们在One Mind Cyberguide所做的，就是从多个维度识别和评估这些产品。

sentences.en: We look at how credible is it?
sentences.zh: 我们考察它的可信度如何？

sentences.en: Does it have science backing that this product actually works?
sentences.zh: 它是否有科学依据证明该产品确实有效？

sentences.en: Is it based off of evidence-based techniques?
sentences.zh: 它是否基于循证技术？

sentences.en: We look at the user experience.
sentences.zh: 我们考察用户体验。

sentences.en: Is it easy to learn, easy to use, easy to navigate?
sentences.zh: 它是否易于学习、易于使用、易于导航？

sentences.en: Is it free from technical glitches?
sentences.zh: 它是否没有技术故障？

sentences.en: And we look at issues around data security and privacy.
sentences.zh: 我们还考察数据安全和隐私方面的问题。

sentences.en: Does the app live up to standards of regulation?
sentences.zh: 该应用程序是否符合监管标准？

sentences.en: Does it keep your data safe?
sentences.zh: 它是否能保证你的数据安全？

sentences.en: Does it not sell your data to third-party individuals?
sentences.zh: 它是否不会将你的数据出售给第三方？

sentences.en: And I think that all these things are things that should figure into a decision on whether
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些因素都应该纳入决策考量，以决定

sentences.en: an app might be a reasonable product for you to try to be able to promote your own mental health and wellness.
sentences.zh: 某个应用程序是否是一个适合你尝试的、能够促进你自身心理健康和福祉的合理产品。

sentences.en: How do you at The Cyberguide decide which apps to review since there are so many out there covering such a range of conditions?
sentences.zh: 既然市面上有这么多涵盖各种病症的应用程序，你们Cyberguide是如何决定评估哪些应用的？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good question when we get asked a lot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个我们经常被问到的好问题。

sentences.en: It's a little bit of an art and a little bit of a science.
sentences.zh: 这既是一门艺术，也是一门科学。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we really want to focus on products that people are using.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们确实想专注于人们正在使用的产品。

sentences.en: So we look at the number of downloads and the use of those products by consumers.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们查看下载量以及消费者对这些产品的使用情况。

sentences.en: We want to focus on products that are backed by science.
sentences.zh: 我们想专注于有科学支持的产品。

sentences.en: And so we constantly are looking at the scientific literature in terms of, you know, what works, what is evidence behind it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在查阅科学文献，看看什么有效，背后有什么证据。

sentences.en: We also want to focus on things that are useful for people.
sentences.zh: 我们也想专注于对人们有用的东西。

sentences.en: And so we focus on products that fit the needs of different consumers.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们专注于满足不同消费者需求的产品。

sentences.en: We have partnerships with various organizations, and they help us figure out what products their constituents are interested in.
sentences.zh: 我们与各个组织建立了合作关系，他们帮助我们了解其成员对哪些产品感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so I think the processes that we use to identify what products that we look at kind of aligns with the ways that people decide to use these things,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们用来确定评估哪些产品的流程，与人们决定使用这些产品的方式是一致的，

sentences.en: that they hear about them from trusted sources, from their doctors, their friends, from family members.
sentences.zh: 即他们从值得信赖的来源、医生、朋友、家人那里听说这些产品。

sentences.en: They read articles about them on social media or in websites, or they might see an advertisement for a product, you know, in a couple of different places.
sentences.zh: 他们通过社交媒体或网站阅读关于它们的文章，或者可能在几个不同的地方看到产品的广告。

sentences.en: And so I think we at One Mind Cyberguide, we're constantly looking at all that information.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们One Mind Cyberguide一直在关注所有这些信息。

sentences.en: And then we prioritize things based off of, again, what people are using and what the science is saying.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们再次根据人们的使用情况和科学研究的结论来确定优先顺序。

sentences.en: Who are your reviewers and what are their qualifications?
sentences.zh: 你们的评估员是谁？他们有什么资质？

sentences.en: How do they become reviewers for the Cyberguide?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何成为Cyberguide的评估员的？

sentences.en: So at One Mind Cyberguide, we have a team of different reviewers in-house that review different products for our website.
sentences.zh: 在One Mind Cyberguide，我们有一个内部评估员团队，专门为我们的网站评估不同的产品。

sentences.en: And those reviewers all undergo training to be able to use the materials we use to be able to evaluate products.
sentences.zh: 这些评估员都接受过培训，能够使用我们所用的材料来评估产品。

sentences.en: We also do some contracting out for some of our review material to outside experts, to clinical psychologists and other mental health professionals.
sentences.zh: 我们也会将部分评估工作外包给外部专家，即临床心理学家和其他心理健康专业人士。

sentences.en: But those are usually what we call professional reviews.
sentences.zh: 但这些通常被称为专业评估。

sentences.en: And so on the One Mind Cyberguide website, in addition to those criteria that I mentioned, the credibility, the user experience, and transparency around data security and privacy,
sentences.zh: 因此，在One Mind Cyberguide网站上，除了我提到的可信度、用户体验以及数据安全和隐私的透明度这些标准外，

sentences.en: we also have sort of a narrative description of how you might use this product in your life.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一种叙述性描述，说明你如何在生活中使用该产品。

sentences.en: And what are the pros and what are some of the pros and cons and what are some of the different clinical considerations.
sentences.zh: 以及它的优点和缺点是什么，还有一些不同的临床考量。

sentences.en: And those narrative reviews are all written by professionals.
sentences.zh: 这些叙述性评估都是由专业人士撰写的。

sentences.en: And so the individuals doing those credibility, user experience,
sentences.zh: 因此，负责可信度、用户体验、

sentences.en: and transparency reviews are all members of the One Mind Cyberguide team that are trained to be able to use those rating scales with fidelity and reliably.
sentences.zh: 以及透明度评估的人员，都是One Mind Cyberguide团队的成员，他们受过培训，能够忠实且可靠地使用这些评分量表。

sentences.en: Do you collect any information from the users and use that as a basis for how you review various products?
sentences.zh: 你们是否会收集用户的信息，并将其作为评估各种产品的基础？

sentences.en: You know, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I think it's something that would be really useful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会非常有用。

sentences.en: It's not something that we actually currently do at One Mind Cyberguide, but definitely something that we have a lot of interest in.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我们目前在One Mind Cyberguide实际做的事情，但绝对是我们非常感兴趣的事情。

sentences.en: And we've done a little bit of that information before, but it's hard to track that.
sentences.zh: 我们以前做过一点点这方面的信息收集，但很难追踪。

sentences.en: And I think that's actually one thing that really necessitates having a product like One Mind Cyberguide is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上是需要像One Mind Cyberguide这样的产品的一个原因，你知道，

sentences.en: you would think about where those consumer reviews often live, and those are in the app stores.
sentences.zh: 你会想到那些消费者评论通常存在于哪里，那就是应用商店。

sentences.en: And so you go to the app store and you see, you know, this person thinks this is a five-star app.
sentences.zh: 所以你去应用商店，看到有人认为这是一个五星级的应用，

sentences.en: This person thinks this is a four-star app.
sentences.zh: 有人认为这是一个四星级的应用。

sentences.en: And what we find is that those ratings and those user ratings from the app stores often don't relate to the credibility and the benefits of those products.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，应用商店里的那些评分和用户评价，往往与产品的可信度和益处无关。

sentences.en: Now, I think there's some problems with the way that those ratings appear in the app store.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为应用商店中这些评分的呈现方式存在一些问题。

sentences.en: So I think that there's a lot of companies that are probably paying people to put positive ratings in the app store or, you know, they're biased.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有很多公司可能在付钱让人在应用商店里给出正面评价，或者，你知道，它们是有偏见的。

sentences.en: So only the people who are having really good experiences are going to the app stores to leave those ratings.
sentences.zh: 所以只有那些有非常好体验的人才会去应用商店留下这些评分。

sentences.en: So I don't mean that to say that I don't think consumer – the impact on consumers and the benefits from consumers and the views of consumers are important.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是说我不认为消费者——消费者受到的影响、消费者的获益以及消费者的观点不重要。

sentences.en: I just think it's a tricky thing to figure out how to collect systematically in an unbiased fashion, like we try to do with the work we do at One Mind Cyberguide.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为，如何以一种无偏见的方式系统地收集这些信息是一件棘手的事情，就像我们试图在One Mind Cyberguide的工作中所做的那样。

sentences.en: And it's something that we're still trying to figure out the best way to be able to incorporate.
sentences.zh: 这是我们仍在努力寻找最佳整合方式的事情。

sentences.en: So I would really hope that that would be something that One Mind Cyberguide would be using in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望这能成为One Mind Cyberguide未来会使用的方式。

sentences.en: But I think it's still a really important open question about how to best collect that information.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，关于如何最好地收集这些信息，仍然是一个非常重要的开放性问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of risky, like using Yelp to choose the restaurant where you want to eat tonight.
sentences.zh: 是的，有点冒险，就像用Yelp来选择你今晚想去吃的餐厅一样。

sentences.en: Well, and I think that's a great point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, I sort of – I love restaurants, so I like the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，我有点——我喜欢餐厅，所以我喜欢这个比喻。

sentences.en: I liked when we used to be able to go to them.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我们过去还能去餐厅的时候。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think what we think about sometimes at Cyberguide is that we sort of are the Michelin star equivalent.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为我们在Cyberguide有时会想，我们有点像是米其林星级的等价物。

sentences.en: So we have experts going.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有专家去评估。

sentences.en: We're trying to figure out, like, at the best, what is this product capable of?
sentences.zh: 我们试图弄清楚，在最好的情况下，这个产品能做到什么程度？

sentences.en: And I think the Yelps are important as well, you know, because there's a lot of information and value that gets added from consumer ratings.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为Yelp也很重要，你知道，因为消费者评分增加了很多信息和价值。

sentences.en: And, you know, Michelin stars and Yelp ratings don't always line up.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，米其林星级和Yelp评分并不总是吻合的。

sentences.en: And I think that we would need both, but I think we need both in a way that sort of acknowledges what are the pros and cons of each approach.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要两者，但我认为我们需要以一种承认每种方法优缺点的方式来使用两者。

sentences.en: If I have a four-and-a-half star rated Taco Bell, I don't think about that as being on the same, you know, standard as a well-reviewed Mexican restaurant that has a Michelin star.
sentences.zh: 如果我看到一家四星半的塔可钟（Taco Bell），我不认为它和一家获得米其林星级、评价良好的墨西哥餐厅处于同一标准。

sentences.en: But maybe that tells me something about that particular location.
sentences.zh: 但这也许能告诉我关于那个特定地点的一些信息。

sentences.en: And so I think bringing that information together, I think, is really valuable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为将这些信息结合起来是非常有价值的。

sentences.en: But again, it has to be done in a way that understands that each of those approaches, the Michelin approach and the Yelp approach, have strengths and limitations.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这样做必须建立在理解每种方法（米其林方法和Yelp方法）都有其优势和局限性的基础上。

sentences.en: And you want to leverage the strengths while downplaying the limitations.
sentences.zh: 你想要利用它们的优势，同时淡化它们的局限性。

sentences.en: How much should consumers rely on apps for their mental health issues?
sentences.zh: 消费者在心理健康问题上应该多大程度上依赖应用程序？

sentences.en: Are there some conditions that are better suited to apps than others?
sentences.zh: 是否有些病症比其他病症更适合使用应用程序？

sentences.en: For example, I can't envision someone with a serious mental health issue, such as, say, schizophrenia, getting much help from an app.
sentences.zh: 例如，我无法想象一个有严重心理健康问题的人，比如精神分裂症患者，能从应用程序中获得多少帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, first I'd like to say that apps are no replacement for a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，首先我想说，应用程序不能替代治疗师。

sentences.en: These are not meant to be replacements for traditional mental health services or for mental health professionals.
sentences.zh: 这些并不旨在替代传统的心理健康服务或心理健康专业人员。

sentences.en: And so I think that there's sometimes a false dichotomy made between apps versus traditional treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有时在应用程序与传统治疗之间存在一种错误的二分法。

sentences.en: And I think that really the best case scenario should be technology plus traditional services, technology and human services.
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的情况应该是技术加传统服务，即技术与人类服务相结合。

sentences.en: When we look at the research, however, though, pretty much anything you can treat through a psychosocial intervention, through traditional treatments,
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们审视研究时，几乎任何可以通过心理社会干预、通过传统治疗来治疗的问题，

sentences.en: you can treat using a digital technology as either in some sort of combination with a human supporter or with some sort of relationship with some human support.
sentences.zh: 你都可以使用数字技术来治疗，要么是与人类支持者结合，要么是与人类支持建立某种关系。

sentences.en: And so there are definitely there are apps out there for psychosis, there are apps out there for bipolar disorder, there are apps out there for a host of serious mental illnesses.
sentences.zh: 所以市面上绝对有针对精神病的应用程序，有针对双相情感障碍的应用程序，也有针对一系列严重精神疾病的应用程序。

sentences.en: I think actually, you know, interesting,
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为，你知道，很有趣的是，

sentences.en: I think one of the products that I'm really interested in when it comes to psychosis and schizophrenia is looking at these cognitive remediation products.
sentences.zh: 我认为在精神病和精神分裂症方面，我非常感兴趣的产品之一是这些认知矫正产品。

sentences.en: So these are technologies that essentially provide brain training to be able to improve the cognitive functioning.
sentences.zh: 所以这些技术本质上是提供大脑训练，以改善认知功能。

sentences.en: And those tools work.
sentences.zh: 这些工具是有效的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of robust scientific evidence behind them.
sentences.zh: 它们背后有大量扎实的科学证据。

sentences.en: But again,
sentences.zh: 但同样，

sentences.en: those aren't seen as a replacement for some of the other pieces that are part of the treatment that an individual with psychosis or schizophrenia might receive to be able to promote their recovery.
sentences.zh: 这些并不被视为替代精神病或精神分裂症患者在康复过程中可能接受的其他治疗部分。

sentences.en: So we find that these tools work for a variety of different people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现这些工具对各种不同的人都有效。

sentences.en: Now, I think depending on the mental health challenge that someone's facing, there might be more or less appropriate uses of these technologies and sort of the continuum of care.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为根据某人面临的心理健康挑战，这些技术在护理连续体中的适用程度可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: So, for example, in the UK, the National Institute for Clinical Excellence actually recommends digital treatments as frontline treatments for the treatment of depression, anxiety.
sentences.zh: 例如，在英国，国家临床优化研究所（NICE）实际上建议将数字治疗作为抑郁症和焦虑症的一线治疗方法。

sentences.en: They don't have that same recommendation for serious mental illness.
sentences.zh: 他们对严重精神疾病没有同样的建议。

sentences.en: And so I think for common mental health issues, these might be very nice sort of frontline treatments or might be ways to sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于常见的心理健康问题，这些可能是非常好的一线治疗方法，或者可能是引入传统心理社会治疗中所教授技能的方式。

sentences.en: really introduce the skills that get taught in traditional psychosocial treatments.
sentences.zh: 但对于更严重的精神疾病，它们可能扮演略有不同的角色。

sentences.en: But for more serious mental illnesses, they might play a slightly different role.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为研究确实支持这些东西在各种病症中都是有用的。

sentences.en: So I think research really supports that these things are useful across a variety of conditions.
sentences.zh: 但我们使用它们的方式可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: But the way that we use them might differ.
sentences.zh: 目前研究生心理学课程中对此教授了多少？

sentences.en: How much is this being taught right now in graduate psychology programs?
sentences.zh: 人们是否正在接受培训，将应用程序作为他们未来可能提供的治疗的一部分？

sentences.en: Are people being trained to use apps as part of the therapy that they may offer in the future?
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是当前临床项目的主要部分，至少没有得到广泛的培训。

sentences.en: I don't think it's a major part of current clinical programs, at least not broadly trained.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这个领域，专业知识仍在发展中。

sentences.en: I think that there's still a developing expertise in this area.
sentences.zh: 我认为在一些地方，我们看到了很多好的工作、培训和实施。

sentences.en: I think there's some places where we see a lot of good work and training and implementation.
sentences.zh: 例如，国防部和退伍军人事务部一直是这些工具开发的先驱。

sentences.en: So, for example, the Department of Defense and the Veterans Administration have been frontrunners, both in the development of these tools.
sentences.zh: 他们是开发一些最早的心理健康应用程序（包括PTSD Coach）的领军专家。

sentences.en: They were leading experts in terms of developing some of the first mental health apps, including PTSD Coach.
sentences.zh: 他们继续拥有一套不同的产品。

sentences.en: And they continue to have a suite of different products.
sentences.zh: 而且因为他们有这么多不同的工具，他们确实在培训国防部和退伍军人事务部的人员在实践中使用这些工具。

sentences.en: And because they have so many different tools, they're really training people in the DOD and VA to use these tools in their practice.
sentences.zh: 但我认为如果你去心理学研究生课程，

sentences.en: But I think if you go to, like, graduate programs in psychology,
sentences.zh: 可能没有多少工作真正致力于教人们如何在临床工作中深思熟虑地使用技术。

sentences.en: there's probably not a lot of work that's really looking at teaching people how to use technology thoughtfully in their clinical work.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个在未来的培训项目中需要解决的重要领域，也是我非常关心的事情，因为我认为，

sentences.en: And so I think this is something that really would be an important area to address in sort of future training programs and is something that I care a lot about because I think that,
sentences.zh: 你知道，再次强调，这不是用技术代替人。

sentences.en: you know, again, this is not technology instead of people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要培养一支受过教育的劳动力队伍，以便在实践中使用这些工具。

sentences.en: And so I think we need to train a workforce that's educated to use these tools in their practice.
sentences.zh: 什么造就了引人入胜的用户体验？

sentences.en: What makes for an engaging user experience?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些应用程序比其他应用程序更具粘性，让用户不断回来使用？

sentences.en: Why are some apps stickier than others and make users come back?
sentences.zh: 如果人们确实系统地使用它们，这难道不会使它们更有效吗？

sentences.en: And doesn't that make them more effective if people actually use them systematically?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为确实如此，使用这些产品的人往往能从中获得更多。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that is the case, that people who use these products tend to get more out of them.
sentences.zh: 我认为参与度科学是一个具有挑战性的领域，因为我认为人们可能不会那么频繁地使用工具，但仍然能从中受益，这是有原因的。

sentences.en: I think that the science of engagement is a challenging area because I think that there are reasons where, you know, people may not use a tool as much and still benefit.
sentences.zh: 例如，可能会出现我称之为“快乐放弃”的情况，即，你知道，我从这个应用程序中得到了我需要的东西，现在我不再需要使用它了。

sentences.en: So, for example, there might be the term I use is happy abandonment, which is, you know, I got what I needed out of this app and now I don't need to use it anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一种机制，即最需要帮助的人往往最频繁地使用该产品或应用程序。

sentences.en: And that there's also some mechanism through which the people who need the most help tend to use the product the most or an app the moSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，临床严重程度与应用程序使用之间存在一种关系，这使得理解参与度和结果之间的关系变得复杂。

sentences.en: And so there's a relationship between clinical severity and app use that sort of complicates understanding of the relationship between engagements and outcomes.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么理解参与度和结果之间的关系变得复杂。

sentences.en: That being said, you know, the only way these things could work is if someone uses it.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，你知道，这些东西能起作用的唯一前提是有人去使用它。

sentences.en: And so I think to answer your question about what makes these apps sticky or engaging or makes people want to come back, I think simplicity is a really sort of important piece.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于你问到的什么让这些应用具有粘性、吸引力，或者让人想回头使用，我认为“简洁”是一个非常重要的因素。

sentences.en: That it has to be a product that's easy to use and that integrates into your life well.
sentences.zh: 它必须是一款易于使用且能很好地融入你生活的产物。

sentences.en: I think a lot of these sort of digital health technologies make people's lives harder by giving them something more to do and none of us need something more to do in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多这类数字健康技术反而让人们的生活变得更艰难，因为它们给人们增加了额外要做的事，而我们谁也不需要生活中再多出些负担。

sentences.en: And so I think the best products are ones that sort of simply and reduce burden and reduce complication by sort of seamlessly integrating to a person's life.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最好的产品是那些能通过无缝融入个人生活，从而简化负担、减少复杂性的产品。

sentences.en: I think also being able to meet the needs of the user.
sentences.zh: 我认为能够满足用户的需求也很重要。

sentences.en: So some people might really want videos and other forms of media to engage in.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能非常需要视频和其他形式的媒体内容来进行互动。

sentences.en: Some people might do well from having very brief sort of exercises to read.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能更适合阅读一些非常简短的练习内容。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think it's also the case that not one app is going to meet the needs of sort of all different users or really appeal to everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为事实也确实如此：没有哪一款应用能满足所有不同用户的需求，或者真正吸引所有人。

sentences.en: And so I think understanding who the app is built for and having the content and the interaction styles and the things that really kind of fit that different person.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为理解这款应用是为谁而建，并拥有真正契合不同人群的内容、互动风格和功能，这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: So I think an important implication of that frame that thinking is that for a consumer, if you're interested in using one of these products, to try a couple of different of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种思维框架的一个重要启示是：如果你作为消费者有兴趣使用这类产品，不妨多尝试几款。

sentences.en: So if you want to use a mindfulness app to download maybe two or three mindfulness apps, try out a couple of the mentations, see which ones really sort of fit your lifestyle,
sentences.zh: 比如你想用一款正念应用，那就下载两三个试试，体验一下其中的一些练习，看看哪些真正适合你的生活方式，

sentences.en: the way you like to engage content, the ones that make sense to you, that you like the color schemes.
sentences.zh: 看看你喜欢的内容互动方式，哪些对你来说有意义，以及你是否喜欢它们的配色方案。

sentences.en: You know, all those things, I think, play a big role.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为所有这些因素都起着很大的作用。

sentences.en: And then to decide to kind of use that product.
sentences.zh: 然后再决定去使用那款产品。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the benefits.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是好处之一。

sentences.en: You know, I kind of introduced this as a challenge.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我刚才把它作为一个挑战提了出来。

sentences.en: It's like there's, you know, 20 to 25,000 things out there.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你知道，市面上有两万到两万五千种这样的东西。

sentences.en: So it's really hard to find ones that are evidence-based.
sentences.zh: 所以要找到有循证依据的产品真的很难。

sentences.en: But I think the flip side of that is because there are so many, that means if you do a little bit of searching,
sentences.zh: 但我认为反过来说，正因为数量如此之多，意味着只要你稍微花点时间搜索，

sentences.en: you might be able to find one that really does fit what you need when you're looking for one of these products.
sentences.zh: 你就有可能找到一款真正符合你需求的产品。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little bit more about data privacy.
sentences.zh: 让我们再多谈谈数据隐私问题。

sentences.en: You mentioned that as being one of the aspects that you look at when you're evaluating apps.
sentences.zh: 你提到这是你在评估应用时会考虑的方面之一。

sentences.en: And there's been a lot of chatter in the news lately about at least one of these big app companies possibly mining user data for marketing purposes.
sentences.zh: 最近新闻里有很多关于至少一家大型应用公司可能为了营销目的挖掘用户数据的讨论。

sentences.en: How much should consumers be worried about this and what can they do to protect themselves?
sentences.zh: 消费者应该对此有多担心？他们又能做些什么来保护自己呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's definitely something consumers should be concerned about.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对是消费者应该关心的问题。

sentences.en: And we did a review where we looked, we took a deep dive into the data security privacy policies of about 120 different apps for depression.
sentences.zh: 我们曾做过一项评估，深入研究了约120款抑郁症相关应用的数据安全与隐私政策。

sentences.en: And we found that about half of those didn't have a data security and privacy policy.
sentences.zh: 我们发现其中约有一半的应用根本没有数据安全和隐私政策。

sentences.en: And of the half that did, only half of those privacy and security policies were what we deemed acceptable.
sentences.zh: 而在有政策的那一半中，只有一半被我们认为是可接受的。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of variance.
sentences.zh: 所以差异非常大。

sentences.en: And there's also a lot of, or I should say there's not a lot of information out there for a lot of these products.
sentences.zh: 而且，或者我应该说，对于很多这类产品，市面上并没有太多相关信息。

sentences.en: So I definitely think that a consumer should read the data security and privacy policy.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对认为消费者应该阅读数据安全和隐私政策。

sentences.en: And look, I know I've looked at a lot of terms and services and privacy policies for different technologies I do.
sentences.zh: 看，我知道我自己也看过很多不同技术的服务条款和隐私政策。

sentences.en: And it's a big wall of text.
sentences.zh: 那简直是一大片密密麻麻的文字墙。

sentences.en: And I just click accept and I move on.
sentences.zh: 我通常就是直接点击“接受”然后继续。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, one thing I think is important, one easy thing to sort of look at is does the product have a data security and privacy policy?
sentences.zh: 但我认为，你知道，有一点很重要，一个简单的检查方法是：该产品是否有数据安全和隐私政策？

sentences.en: Because I mentioned many don't.
sentences.zh: 因为我提到过，很多产品都没有。

sentences.en: And so I think that's a red flag in itself.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这本身就是一个危险信号。

sentences.en: If they don't tell you what they're doing with your data, you probably don't like it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不告诉你他们如何处理你的数据，你大概不会喜欢这样。

sentences.en: You know, as I mentioned, those Department of Defense and VA apps,
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如我提到的，那些国防部和退伍军人事务部的应用，

sentences.en: I think those are very good apps with very good data security and privacy policies because they are developed by the VA and the DOD.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们是非常好的应用，有着非常好的数据安全和隐私政策，因为它们是由退伍军人事务部和国防部开发的。

sentences.en: And so they don't collect the type of information that some of these other products collect that are potentially using you as a revenue generating source when you're using their product.
sentences.zh: 所以它们不会收集其他一些产品所收集的那类信息，那些产品在用户使用时，可能正把用户当作创收来源。

sentences.en: And so I think looking at where the app comes from is important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为关注应用的来源很重要。

sentences.en: I think, you know, the other thing to consider is, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，另一件要考虑的事情是，你知道，

sentences.en: everyone is a little bit different in terms of their sense of what data is being collected from them and how comfortable they are with that.
sentences.zh: 每个人对于自己被收集了什么数据以及对此的接受程度，都有所不同。

sentences.en: So I fully appreciate that when I use Google Maps, Google knows where I'm going all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我完全理解，当我使用谷歌地图时，谷歌随时都知道我要去哪里。

sentences.en: And that's a tradeoff I'm willing to make because, you know, I'm not going anywhere that's all that exciting.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我愿意做的权衡，因为，你知道，我去的也不是什么特别令人兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: And I really like to use Google Maps.
sentences.zh: 而且我真的很喜欢用谷歌地图。

sentences.en: And so I think that if we think about data and privacy as somewhat transactional, that a person can be hopefully make an informed decision whether the transaction,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果我们把数据和隐私看作是一种交易，那么一个人如果能做出知情决定，判断这种交易，

sentences.en: the benefit they get from that product is worth whatever they're giving up or potentially giving up when they're using that product.
sentences.zh: 即他们从产品中获得的利益是否值得他们在使用产品时所放弃或可能放弃的东西，那就再好不过了。

sentences.en: And that's one reason why we actually call our data security and privacy scale a transparency scale, because to us,
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我们实际上把我们的数据安全和隐私评分称为“透明度评分”，因为对我们来说，

sentences.en: it's really the important piece is the transparency of the information such that a consumer can make an informed decision of whether what information is being collected from them is worth the benefit they're receiving from using that product.
sentences.zh: 真正重要的是信息的透明度，这样消费者才能做出知情决定：收集的信息是否值得他们从使用该产品中获得的利益。

sentences.en: So what are some of the best mental health apps out there for various conditions?
sentences.zh: 那么，针对各种病症，目前市面上最好的心理健康应用有哪些？

sentences.en: I mean, I know there's no one size fits all answers, but there must be some that rise above the reSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道没有万能的答案，但肯定有一些产品脱颖而出吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think that it's a challenging question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为这是一个很有挑战性的问题。

sentences.en: And definitely one thing that we do at One Mind Cyberguide is we don't endorse any specific product.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在One Mind Cyberguide所做的一件事就是，我们绝对不会为任何特定产品背书。

sentences.en: We have our scores and we sort of, you know, emphasize, you know, what I've noted for you is that there's different ways to evaluate these things.
sentences.zh: 我们有我们的评分，我们只是，你知道，强调，你知道，我为你指出的，评估这些东西有不同的方法。

sentences.en: And there's different aspects that people might care about.
sentences.zh: 而且人们可能关心的方面也各不相同。

sentences.en: So someone might care a lot about credibility.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人可能非常关心可信度。

sentences.en: I really want to know that this works and might be kind of technically savvy.
sentences.zh: 我真的想知道这是否有效，而且他们可能在技术上比较精通。

sentences.en: And so they're a little bit less concerned about the user experience.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对用户体验的关注度会稍微低一些。

sentences.en: On the flip side, maybe someone is more open to a tool that doesn't have as much science behind it if it's really engaging and they like it and it's, you know,
sentences.zh: 反过来，也许有人更愿意尝试一种科学依据没那么充分的工具，如果它真的很有吸引力，他们很喜欢，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: really sticky for them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说非常有粘性。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think, again, there's a lot of diversity in terms of what fits for, you know, specific people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为，再次强调，对于特定的人来说，什么才是合适的，这存在很大的多样性。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that, as I mentioned, those VA, DOD apps are, you know, they have a lot of evidence behind them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，正如我提到的，那些退伍军人事务部和国防部的应用，你知道，它们背后有很多循证依据。

sentences.en: We really like them.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很喜欢它们。

sentences.en: You know, so like PTSD Coach, there's a COVID Coach app that kind of focuses on stress and anxiety related to COVID.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如PTSD Coach，还有一个COVID Coach应用，它主要关注与新冠相关的压力和焦虑。

sentences.en: These apps do lean a little bit more towards veterans.
sentences.zh: 这些应用确实更偏向退伍军人。

sentences.en: And so there's a little bit more of that flavor in some of their content sometimes, which might be a barrier for some people.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的一些内容有时会带有那种色彩，这对某些人来说可能是一个障碍。

sentences.en: But I think what's great about those apps is that you know that they're based on evidence-based practices.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些应用很棒的地方在于，你知道它们是基于循证实践的。

sentences.en: They have a solid clinical and development team behind them and that you know that they work really well.
sentences.zh: 它们背后有扎实的临床和开发团队，而且你知道它们的效果非常好。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, for a variety of other apps, there are things that, you know, maybe kind of align with what you're kind of looking to get.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，对于其他各种应用，有些东西，你知道，可能与你想要获得的东西相符。

sentences.en: So, for example, our group has been looking at mood tracking apps recently.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们小组最近一直在研究情绪追踪应用。

sentences.en: I really like a mood tracking app called Daleo because it kind of lets me track my moods in a way that's really useful for me.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢一款叫Daleo的情绪追踪应用，因为它让我能以一种对我非常有用的方式追踪我的情绪。

sentences.en: But that might not be useful for everybody.
sentences.zh: 但这可能对每个人都不一定有用。

sentences.en: So, you know, I really do sort of encourage, as I noted before, that one of the best ways to kind of find an app that might work for you, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我确实非常鼓励，正如我之前提到的，找到可能适合你的应用的最佳方法之一，你知道，

sentences.en: go to the One Mind Cyberguide website, poke around a little bit, maybe find two or three apps in an area, you know, two or three meditation apps that seem like the best picks.
sentences.zh: 去One Mind Cyberguide网站，随便逛逛，也许在一个领域找两三个应用，你知道，两三个看起来是最佳选择的正念应用。

sentences.en: So, maybe you pick Headspace, Calm, and Insight Timer.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许你选择了Headspace、Calm和Insight Timer。

sentences.en: You look at those different products and you see which one kind of fits best for you.
sentences.zh: 你看看这些不同的产品，看看哪一个最适合你。

sentences.en: And I think that's really an approach that we sort of advocate in terms of trying to figure out which app a person might end up using to be able to help promote their mental health and wellness.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是我们所倡导的方法，即试图找出一个人最终可能会使用哪种应用，来帮助促进他们的心理健康和福祉。

sentences.en: I know the health insurance company that I have at work has given us access to at least one mental health app for free, which you would normally pay for.
sentences.zh: 我知道我公司购买的健康保险为我们免费提供至少一款心理健康应用，而这通常是需要付费的。

sentences.en: Is that something that's on the increase where insurance companies are also promoting these apps?
sentences.zh: 保险公司也在推广这些应用，这种趋势在增加吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's definitely the case.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: We actually just did a review of that through One Mind Cyberguide and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上刚刚通过One Mind Cyberguide对此进行了评估，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: looked at a couple different insurance companies and found that there were a lot of different products that they were providing.
sentences.zh: 查看了几家不同的保险公司，发现他们提供的产品种类繁多。

sentences.en: Although, you know, nowhere near as vast as the 25,000 I know that are out there.
sentences.zh: 虽然，你知道，远没有我所知道的市面上那25,000种那么多。

sentences.en: So, probably about like half a dozen or half a dozen to a dozen products that different insurance companies were providing.
sentences.zh: 所以，大概有六到十二种左右的产品是不同的保险公司提供的。

sentences.en: My insurance company actually provides one as well.
sentences.zh: 我的保险公司实际上也提供了一款。

sentences.en: So, I just got a notification that MyStrength, which is a cognitive behavioral therapy app, is available through my insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚收到通知，MyStrength，一款认知行为疗法应用，可以通过我的保险使用。

sentences.en: And so, that is something worth looking at is that if you have insurance and are covered,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有保险并且在承保范围内，这确实值得一看，

sentences.en: there might be a product that your insurance is covering that there would usually be a payment associated with it.
sentences.zh: 可能有一款你的保险正在承保的产品，通常是需要付费的。

sentences.en: But you might be able to receive it for free.
sentences.zh: 但你也许可以免费获得它。

sentences.en: And then, additionally, sometimes these are products that are not publicly available on the app store.
sentences.zh: 此外，有时这些产品在应用商店里并不是公开可用的。

sentences.en: So, you may not be able to go download it yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能无法自己去下载它。

sentences.en: They usually go through enterprise contracts to companies or insurance companies, insurance providers.
sentences.zh: 它们通常通过企业合同提供给公司或保险公司、保险提供商。

sentences.en: And so, you might have some access to some products you might not be able to find on your own through your insurance company.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过你的保险公司，你可能会获得一些你自己可能找不到的产品的使用权。

sentences.en: In a recent paper that you published, you wrote about three misconceptions about digital mental health.
sentences.zh: 在你最近发表的一篇论文中，你写到了关于数字心理健康的三个误区。

sentences.en: And one of those misconceptions was that mental health technologies are a new way to deliver psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 其中一个误区是：心理健康技术是提供心理治疗的一种新方式。

sentences.en: Why is that a misconception if digital mental health is not a new way to deliver therapy?
sentences.zh: 如果数字心理健康不是提供治疗的新方式，为什么这是一个误区？

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那它是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that technology offers a lot of opportunities to do things in a new and different way.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为技术确实提供了很多以新颖和不同方式做事的机会。

sentences.en: And so, I think that if we are merely translating traditional practices from therapy to technology,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为如果我们仅仅是将传统的治疗实践转化为技术，

sentences.en: we are doing a disservice to individuals who might be able to be better reached and better served by new technology.
sentences.zh: 我们就是在损害那些本可以通过新技术得到更好接触和服务的人。

sentences.en: So, for example, let me make sort of a metaphor here is that a lot of these early technologies came out.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，让我打个比方，很多早期的技术刚出来时，

sentences.en: When they came out, they really had this sort of like session frame of thinking that was present in sort of psychotherapy practice.
sentences.zh: 它们确实有一种存在于心理治疗实践中的“疗程”思维框架。

sentences.en: So, it's like you log on to the website, you do your 50-minute session.
sentences.zh: 就像你登录网站，进行50分钟的疗程。

sentences.en: So, you know, you read something for a couple of minutes, then you do some exercises.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你读几分钟的东西，然后做一些练习。

sentences.en: And then you have to wait until next week to get your next session.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须等到下周才能进行下一次疗程。

sentences.en: And that's not the way people use technologies.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是人们使用技术的方式。

sentences.en: We're like, we're in Netflix.
sentences.zh: 我们就像是在用Netflix。

sentences.en: We're in an on-demand world.
sentences.zh: 我们处于一个点播的世界。

sentences.en: You want things now and you want things in the moment.
sentences.zh: 你想要现在就得到东西，你想要在当下就得到东西。

sentences.en: You know, if I wanted to learn how to cook an omelet and I signed up for a – you know, went to the web and signed up for a class, it would be ridiculous to say that like, okay,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我想学怎么做煎蛋卷，然后我注册了一个——你知道，上网注册了一个课程，如果有人说：“好吧，史蒂芬，等一周，我们教你怎么敲鸡蛋。”那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: well, Stephen, wait a week and we'll teach you how to crack eggs.
sentences.zh: “再等一周，我们教你怎么煮鸡蛋。”

sentences.en: And wait another week and we'll teach you how to cook them.
sentences.zh: 我想要一个YouTube视频，它能立刻展示给我看怎么做煎蛋卷，而且我想在15分钟内吃上那个煎蛋卷。

sentences.en: I want a YouTube video that's going to show me I'd make an omelet right here and I want to be eating that omelet in 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为技术有潜力更好地创造这些按需的、现实世界的体验。

sentences.en: And so I think that technology has the potential to sort of better create these on-demand, real-world experiences.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引出了一些我们需要进一步评估的开放性问题。

sentences.en: And I think that those lead to some open questions that we have to sort of further evaluate.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道——所以我认为我们需要思考临床实践和行为改变技术，

sentences.en: I think that, you know – so I think that we need to think about how clinical practices and behavior change techniques,
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的科学知识如何转化为技术。

sentences.en: how the science of what we know what works can be translated to technologies.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不能仅仅制造心理治疗的数字版本，因为那可能是技术所能实现的最无聊的用途了。

sentences.en: And I think we can't merely make a digital version of psychotherapy because that's kind of probably the most boring use of what technology is capable of.
sentences.zh: 除了你在心理健康应用方面的工作，你还对技术与心理健康的交叉领域感兴趣。

sentences.en: Beyond your work with mental health apps, you're also interested in the intersection of technology and mental health.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我们一直在谈论的内容。

sentences.en: I think that's what we've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 你最近合著了一份关于青少年、社交媒体和心理健康的报告，

sentences.en: You recently co-authored a report on teens, social media,
sentences.zh: 建议研究人员以细致入微的方式看待这个话题，而不仅仅是问社交媒体对青少年是好是坏。

sentences.en: and mental health that suggested that researchers look at the topic in nuanced ways and not just ask whether social media is good or bad for youth.
sentences.zh: 你能多谈谈那份报告以及你的发现吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit more about that report and what you found?
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 我认为现在有很多担忧——考虑到每个人花在屏幕前的时间之多，我认为这种担忧是有道理的——关于屏幕和社交媒体可能对人们心理健康产生的影响。

sentences.en: I think that there is a lot of concern – I think reasonably so right now with as much time as everyone spending in front of these screens – about the impact that screens and social media might be having on people's mental health.
sentences.zh: 我认为更具体地说，有些人担心社交媒体使用率的增加导致了抑郁、焦虑和自杀等问题的增加。

sentences.en: And I think sort of more specifically some concerns that the increased rates of social media use are leading to increased rates of things like depression, anxiety, and suicide.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我认为我们纵观各项研究发现，研究结果并没有证实这种关系。

sentences.en: I want to just say that I think what we've seen looking across the research is that the research is not bearing out that relationship.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体的使用在平均水平或整体上似乎并没有导致这些问题的增加。

sentences.en: It does not seem that social media use on average or at a whole is leading to the increased rates of these things.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里面有很多细微差别，有些人从社交媒体中受益，有些人受到伤害，

sentences.en: I think that there is a lot of nuance there that some people are helped by social media, some people are hurt,
sentences.zh: 而对于很多人来说，就目前的心理健康和福祉而言，它可能并没有产生多大影响。

sentences.en: and a lot of people it's probably not doing much of anything when it comes to their mental health and wellness right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一点非常重要，我们在报告中也谈到了这一点，而且我认为在重新定义这场辩论方面很重要，那就是“屏幕时间”作为一个概念，在我们目前使用技术的方式中并没有太大的意义。

sentences.en: I think one thing that is really important and that we talk about that in the report and I think is important in terms of reframing the debate is that screen time as a concept doesn't have a lot of meaningfulness in the current way we use technology.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如使用Instagram或Twitter一小时是什么样的？

sentences.en: So like what does an hour of use of Instagram or Twitter look like?
sentences.zh: 你在阅读一些内容。

sentences.en: You're reading some content.
sentences.zh: 你在创作一些内容。

sentences.en: You're creating some content.
sentences.zh: 你在贡献一些内容。

sentences.en: You're contributing some content.
sentences.zh: 你在和一些人进行直接消息沟通。

sentences.en: You're direct messaging with some people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们指出的事情之一是，用我们看待电视节目、广播节目的方式来看待屏幕时间，

sentences.en: And so I think that one of the sort of things that we sort of note is that to think about screen time in the same way we thought about it with TV shows, radio shows,
sentences.zh: 在内容更加碎片化、你所吸收的东西在这样一个新世界里是完全不同的，因为你正在不断地与这些不同的技术进行互动。

sentences.en: things where content is much more chunked and something that you absorb is really different in this new world where you're sort of constantly interacting with these different technologies.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要更好的方法来理解一个人在与这些平台互动时到底在做什么。

sentences.en: And so that we need better ways to sort of understand what is a person actually doing on these platforms when they are interacting with them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多地思考：在这些不同的技术平台上，哪些活动是有助于健康的，哪些活动是有损健康的。

sentences.en: And we need to sort of think more about like what are the wellness facilitating activities and what are the wellness detrimental activities that might take place on these different technology platforMs.
sentences.zh: 你认为技术，不仅仅是应用，在心理健康领域的未来会怎样？

sentences.en: What do you think the future holds for the use of technology and not just apps for the field of mental health?
sentences.zh: 你认为对于心理学领域和消费者来说，未来什么是有帮助的？

sentences.en: What do you think would be helpful going forward, both for the field of psychology and also for consumers?
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的认为在10到20年后，我们将不再谈论“数字健康”或“数字心理健康”。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really think that in 10 to 20 years from now, we're not going to be talking about digital health or digital mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们将谈论使用技术的健康和心理健康方式。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about health and mental health and ways that uses technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为技术将深深融入我们看到的服务交付和触达人们的方式中。

sentences.en: I think that technology is going to become deeply integrated into the way that we see services delivered and see people reached.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，当前的疫情确实正在加速这一进程。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, the current pandemic is really accelerating that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们已经看到远程医疗和虚拟就诊的使用率有了真正的提升。

sentences.en: I think we've seen a real uptake in the use of telehealth and virtual visits.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们已经看到远程医疗和虚拟就诊的使用率有了真正的提升。

sentences.en: And I think to me, the next stage is really thinking about how we create those kind of, you know, as we were talking about a little bit earlier,
sentences.zh: 我认为对我而言，下一个阶段确实是在思考我们如何创造那些，正如我们刚才稍微讨论过的那样，

sentences.en: those new sort of experiences using technology.
sentences.zh: 那些利用科技创造的新型体验。

sentences.en: I think that there's a lot of sort of exciting opportunities for things like virtual reality, augmented reality, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为在虚拟现实、增强现实等领域存在许多令人兴奋的机会，你知道，

sentences.en: different technologies that really make these things much more pervasive and persuasive in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 不同的技术确实能让这些事物在人们的生活中变得更加普及和具有说服力。

sentences.en: And it wouldn't surprise me if in a lot of instances that the first door,
sentences.zh: 如果说在很多情况下，人们在考虑接受心理健康服务，

sentences.en: a lot of people walk through when they think about receiving mental health services or using a tool to sort of promote their wellness or well-being is really a digital tool firSt.
sentences.zh: 或者使用某种工具来促进自身健康与福祉时，首先接触到的往往是数字工具，我一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I think that these are really scale, potentially scalable, cost effective and effective resources.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些资源确实具有规模化潜力，且经济高效、效果显著。

sentences.en: And I think that we'll see a lot more use of these and the sort of continuum of mental health care and wellness support.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将会在心理健康护理和健康支持的连续谱中看到这些工具的更多应用。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us today, Dr. Shuler.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢您今天能来参加我们的节目，Shuler博士。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting and I hope it's going to be edifying to our listeners.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有趣，我希望它能对我们的听众有所启发。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It was great to be on the program.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能参加这个节目。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站speakingofpsychology.org或任何您获取播客的平台上找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何评论或想法，可以发送电子邮件至speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 地址是speakingofpsychology，连在一起，后面接@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由Lee Weinerman制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频编辑是Chris Kondayan。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是Kim Mills。
